summary.one_liner: Jeedom core is a free, open source, multi-protocol home automation platform that centralizes connected devices and runs without external servers.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes Jeedom as a free, open source, multi-protocol home automation software for centralizing and managing connected devices. It states that it does not require access to external servers to function. Users build automations with scenarios, and widgets, views and designs are offered for building the interface. The core acts as the central engine, and features for specific hardware and needs come from plugins, which can be official, third-party, or from the Jeedom Market. The README points to documentation covering installation on 64-bit Debian Linux, scenarios, widgets, users, backups, and plugin development.
use_cases: Centralize smart home devices in one interface
Run a privacy-focused local smart home server
Design custom dashboards and widgets for home controls
Extend the system with plugins for specific hardware
Schedule and configure remote or local backups
how_to_run: Follow the installation guides in the Jeedom documentation for a 64-bit Debian Linux system
notable: Runs without access to external servers, for privacy
Multi-protocol device support through the core and plugins
Customizable interface via widgets, views, and CSS/Javascript
Plugin ecosystem with an official Jeedom Market and third-party plugins
caveats: Installation guides cover 64-bit Debian Linux systems
Device support depends on which plugins are installed
keywords: control smart devices in one place
